corrections: 1) Buzz CAS is not a single 'INSERT ... WHERE current_head = expected_head': it is a write transaction that takes a per-channel advisory lock, reads the head, compares it with the expected revision and only then inserts; same semantics, different mechanism. 2) 'The losing text stays in history' is overstated: a rejected save is rolled back and not stored; only accepted (later superseded) revisions remain in history. 3) GrokBot room canvases are written by agents through a WriteCanvas tool (full contents, no expected revision) and read by humans as a rendered bundle; human co-authoring is not evidenced. The lock/renew/release and tombstone/undelete RPCs belong to the agent file store, not room canvases, and locks return a lease lock_token with TTL; calling them 'fencing tokens' is an over-reach (FENCED is a sandbox manifest commit status). 4) 'CRDT co-edit' for Slack and Teams is inference: Slack's sync engine is undocumented in the evidence and Teams Loop uses the Fluid Framework (ordered ops); say 'real-time co-editing'. 'Block-anchored comments' for Slack is not in the cited evidence (comments behave like thread replies with resolve). 5) Teams evidence is meeting/chat notes (Loop), a weak analogue of a room canvas.
caveats: Slack canvas is DOC-only; channel canvases were retired in favour of a canvas tab (2025); free plan one canvas per conversation
